item.title: Birds battling jet lag: Manx shearwaters suffer jet lag impacting homeward flights; could lead to serious consequences for inexperienced navigators
item.description: Recent research highlights that Manx shearwaters returning from foraging encounters navigational challenges akin to human jet lag. Prolonged flights disrupt their internal clocks, causing misalignment with the local time, which results in notable directional inaccuracies, particularly among novice birds. Analysis of two decades of GPS data from over 1,000 nesting shearwaters underscores these findings. Further investigation is required to assess how this temporal discrepancy may affect additional behaviors.

item.title: 124-year-old handwritten deed sparks oil and gas ownership battle in US; court rules descendants get just one-sixteenth share
item.description: A handwritten property deed from 1902 became the center of a legal dispute over mineral rights. The Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia upheld an appellate ruling regarding the deed's interpretation. The case involved claims to ownership of oil and gas beneath a 117.55-acre property. The court concluded that the Severin family retained one-sixteenth of the oil and gas rights, not one-half.

item.title: Ohio man, 78, visits all 50 US state fairs in retirement, with 19 still to go
item.description: At the age of 75, Jim Chew was ready for new adventures after retirement. With 31 state fairs already visited, he set a goal to explore all 50 by 2030. Each fair offers him a taste of local culture, foods, and a chance to connect with diverse communities. Jim's organized excursions aim to enrich his journey across the nation, filling his days with exciting experiences instead of monotony.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Over 28 cyclists carry Thanksgiving turkeys on their bikes in Maine; unusual ride helps 58 families get free holiday dinners
item.description: More than 28 cyclists participated in the eighth annual Turkey Ride to deliver Thanksgiving turkeys. They gathered at Maine Sport Rockport and picked up items from Hannaford Supermarkets. After collecting donations, they transported the groceries to the Camden Area Christian Food Pantry. Fifty-eight families benefited from the food pantry's effort, receiving turkeys for their Thanksgiving meals. The event highlighted community support for those in need and encouraged charitable involvement.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: After 100 years of extinction, baby oysters found in Scottish estuary; 140,000 adults returned over 12 years
item.description: After more than 100 years, scientists found young European flat oysters in Dornoch Firth, indicating successful natural breeding and conservation. The project aimed to restore native oyster populations through the introduction of adult oysters, totaling around 140,000, over 12 years. Restoration efforts have shown progress as oysters are now reproducing naturally in their habitat. The project supports marine biodiversity by enhancing ecosystems through oyster reef formation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 103-year-old D-Day veteran receives replacement medals 80 years after returning his uniform
item.description: Douglas Halley, a 103-year-old D-Day veteran, recently received his wartime medals which were lost in 1945. A young historian, Joseph Smith, discovered Halley's military record while researching veterans' stories and assisted in recovering the medals. The Ministry of Defence located and mailed the medals back to Halley just before Remembrance Day. This story highlights the importance of remembering personal histories and the sacrifices of war.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Man finds centuries-old gold ring after 15 minutes of metal detecting
item.description: Kevin Short found a centuries-old gold ring inscribed “I live in hope” just 15 minutes into a metal-detecting search in Warwickshire. Authenticated by the British Museum, the 16th-to-18th-century ring is expected to fetch up to £3,000 at a December 2 auction.

item.title: At 102, WWII veteran who helped liberate Dachau receives France’s Legion of Honor; still drives and lives independently
item.description: At 102 years old, William Lyford received France's prestigious Legion of Honor, honoring his bravery during World War II, particularly his role in liberating Dachau concentration camp in 1945. The touching ceremony held in Woodstock was filled with family, friends, and fellow veterans celebrating his significant contributions. Despite his service, Lyford’s daughter shared how he rarely discussed his military past, showcasing the lasting bond between the U.S. and France.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Watch: Massive waves lash California coastline, forces closure of several piers
item.description: California's coastline recently faced towering waves that caused significant damage and led to the temporary closure of several renowned piers. With the National Weather Service alerting residents and tourists about dangerous rip currents, safety recommendations were put in place. Some beaches in Southern California saw seawater flooding, prompting evacuation advisories.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: 'Perfectly safe' but not 'maxed out'? Trump takes Qatar jet to Asia
item.description: US President Donald Trump is set to travel to Asia on Monday aboard the aircraft gifted by Qatar, even as questions remain over its promised security upgrades. According to NBC News, the jet has received some maintenance and cosmetic improvements, but the larger overhaul remains unclear months after an Iran-related security scare forced Trump to fly home from Turkey on a secret military plane.

Amazon loses 40 Leo satellites as ULA's Vulcan rocket fails minutes after launch
item.description: Amazon's planned launch of 40 satellites for its Leo internet network failed after the Vulcan rocket malfunctioned. The Vulcan rocket, operated by United Launch Alliance, experienced an anomaly 10 minutes after liftoff. This failure poses a setback for Amazon's satellite internet plans, which aim to compete with Elon Musk's Starlink. Amazon has also invested in other launch options including Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket and Arianespace.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: 'Not Cuba or Venezuela': Iran warns it will not wait for US attack before responding
item.description: Iran has expressed that it is ready for potential military action while discussing diplomatic avenues with the United States. Deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi indicated three possible scenarios: diplomatic talks, economic blockades, and military response. Tehran has set specific conditions, including ending the war and lifting economic sanctions for any agreement. The arrival of the USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East adds to ongoing regional tensions.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Georgia woman wins $2.5m after rear-end crash leads to spinal fusion surgery
item.description: A woman from Georgia received a substantial $2.5 million settlement for severe neck injuries resulting from a car accident in 2023. The incident occurred when her vehicle was rear-ended while awaiting at a traffic light. Following the crash, she underwent significant medical interventions, including spinal surgery. Her legal team emphasized how these injuries drastically altered her quality of life, highlighting the profound consequences of personal injuries.
